# Fixtures — synthetic, schema unverified

**None of these files was recorded from a live service.** The sandbox in which the crate
was written cannot reach any catalogue. Every file was written by hand (a few through a
small script, to get byte-exact encodings) to the response format each API documents, as
remembered and as described in `docs/research/01-isbn-databases.md`. A fixture can
therefore encode a wrong assumption about the real service: treat a passing test as
"the parser does what we believe the API needs", not as "the API works this way".

To check them against reality and replace them, see "Re-recording fixtures" in the crate
README (`examples/record-fixtures.rs`, `EBC_LIVE=1`). Real recordings may be committed
only for open (class A) sources, with their URL and retrieval date; keep Google Books
fixtures synthetic.

## Books

| ISBN | Book | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| 9782070360024 (2-07-036002-4) | *L'Étranger*, Albert Camus, Gallimard, collection Folio | French title; every provider |
| 9783596294312 | *Die Verwandlung*, Franz Kafka, S. Fischer — the ISBN, record numbers and edition details are invented | German title (DNB, K10plus, lobid, Google Books) |
| 9780141439518 | *Pride and Prejudice*, Jane Austen, Penguin Classics | English title (Library of Congress, Open Library, Wikidata) |
| 9780061120084 | "Reading the Absurd" — an invented scholarly book with a DOI under Crossref's test prefix 10.5555 | Crossref |
| 9782080700124 | "Un autre livre" — invented | "the answer is about another ISBN" |

Record identifiers (ARK, PPN, OLID, Q-id, volume id), prices, dates of last modification
and secondary contributors (preface writers, the Finnish translator, the illustrator of
the second SUDOC record) are invented.

## Files

- `common/` — an HTML error page and a JSON "too many requests" body, served to every
  provider with statuses 429, 502 and 503.
- `<provider>/…` — a found record per language where the source is relevant, "not found"
  in the service's own form, the service's own error envelope (SRU diagnostic, Google
  error object, Finna and Crossref status), an answer about another ISBN, a record with
  most fields missing, and odd encodings: `bnf/etranger-latin1.xml` is ISO-8859-1,
  `bnf/etranger-unimarc.xml` and `dnb/verwandlung.xml` carry the NSB/NSE control
  characters U+0098 and U+009C around articles, `loc/pride.xml` has a decomposed accent,
  `sudoc/record-*.xml` use the PICA `@` filing mark.

Truncated and garbage bodies are generated by `tests/robustness.rs` from these files.
